history.summary: Modern South Indian-style temple at Shivnagar, Narayan Nagar, Latur (413531). It is set in landscaped gardens with an artificial fountain, and the garden houses a roughly 9-foot-tall statue of Lord Shiva. The sanctum holds eight idols of Lord Ganesha, each representing a different form, plus a 4-foot-tall marble Ganesha idol. NOTE: this is a local modern temple and is NOT one of the canonical eight Ashta Vinayaka pilgrimage temples of Maharashtra (those lie in Pune, Ahmednagar and Raigad districts). Founding date, builder and trust details are unverified; opening hours not found in any consulted source.

name: Shri Ashtavinayak Mandir
town_description: Latur is a city in the Marathwada region of Maharashtra, known as a regional education hub and part of the state's sugar belt. Its landmarks include the 12th-century Siddheshwar Ratneshwar temple complex and the 1917 Ganj Golai market, where 15 streets converge on a central roundabout housing the Devi Jagdamba temple. The district was devastated by the 1993 Killari earthquake, after which much of the city was rebuilt.
